This holds because a newly minted alias starts worthless, so the attacker must first farm credibility on each one before it can swing a verdict. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock. Consider a velvet as the anchor of the cost.
